definitions.explanation: A seasoning made by combining vinegar with sugar (and sometimes other ingredients). Used widely in Japanese and Chinese-style cooking for dressings, dipping sauces, and marinades.

examples.japanese: {大根|だいこん}の{甘酢|あまず}{漬|づ}けを{作|つく}った。
{鶏肉|とりにく}を{揚|あ}げて{甘酢|あまず}あんをかけると、{子|こ}どもにも{人気|にんき}のおかずになる。
examples.english: If you deep-fry chicken and pour sweet-and-sour sauce over it, it becomes a dish popular even with children.

notes:
USAGE:
{甘酢|あまず} is a compound of {甘|あま}い (sweet) and {酢|す} (vinegar). It is a basic seasoning combination in Japanese cooking.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {甘酢|あまず}{漬|づ}け (sweet-vinegar pickles)
- {甘酢|あまず}あん (sweet-and-sour thickened sauce)
- {甘酢|あまず}ソース (sweet-and-sour sauce)
- {甘酢|あまず}をかける (pour sweet vinegar over)

COOKING NOTE:
Basic {甘酢|あまず} is made by dissolving sugar in rice vinegar. Variations include adding soy sauce, dashi, or chili. It is used for {南蛮漬|なんばんづ}け (nanban-style marinated dishes) and {酢|す}の{物|もの} (vinegared dishes).
